newsitem.title: USA: Cooler long-term outlook in Brazil coffee belt - WSC.
newsitem.headline: Cooler long-term outlook in Brazil coffee belt - WSC.

text.p: Warm, high pressure aloft Brazil's coffee belt will continue to prevent cool air from moving into the area during the next seven days, although the longer term outlook suggests colder temperatures during the weekend of Aug 9, Weather Services Corp said.
"The very unreliable eight to 10-day extended range charts suggest much colder weather could be headed into the coffee belt during the weekend of Aug 9-10," WSC said in an update on Wednesday.
"We will continue to keep an eye on this forecast change in pattern," it added. "However, at this time we would rate any chance of damaging cold at less than 10 percent."

Fair to partly cloudy skies were observed over main growing areas of the belt this morning. Temperatures remained near normal levels with lows in the low 50's F (low teens C), with some 40 F (5-9 C) in the higher elevations.

WSC said fair to partly cloudy skies are expected during the next seven days in major growing areas of Sao Paulo and Minas Gerias. Temperatures should will be near to above normal, with lows in the 50's to low 60's F (low to middle teens C). Some cooler conditions may hit higher elevations, but no damaging cold is expected, it said.
